# beowulf-fitt-37 — cruces worth recording in QUESTIONS.md

Each: line · word · what was chosen · why disputed or guessed.

- 2694 · `[gefrægn]` · verb supplied by Kemble, "I [heard]"; the MS line has none. `andlongne` "upright" (guess; also "continuous, throughout").
- 2697 · `ne hēdde … þæs heafolan` · "did not heed the head", read as a contrast with Beowulf's blow on the head (2677–80); an inference, not stated.
- 2698 · `mǣges` · MS `mægenes` "of strength"; Kemble `mǣges` "kinsman's" followed, object of `healp` (genitive after a verb that normally takes the dative).
- 2699–2701 · `þæt … þæt ðæt … þæt ðæt` · kept as printed ("so that … so that the … so that the"); Kemble, Thorpe, Rieger `þā` for `þæt` at 2699; Sievers and Holthausen cancel the first `ðæt` (2700); Grundtvig, Sievers, Sedgefield `þā ðæt` (2701).
- 2703 · `wæll-seaxe` · kept as dative-instrumental after `gebrǣd`; E. Sc., Holthausen, Sedgefield `-seax`.
- 2706 · `Fēond gefyldan` · plural verb, two killers; E. Sc., Thorpe, Sievers, Sedgefield `gefylde` (singular).
- 2706 · `ferh ellen wræc` · "courage drove out life", taken as the dragon's life (guess; could be the heroes' own life driven on); Kemble `ferh-ellen`, Kluge `ealne` for `ellen`, Aantekeningen `ellor`.
- 2707 · `ābroten` · Kemble's emendation of MS `abreoten`; sense unchanged.
- 2709–11 · `sīðas[t] sigehwīla … worlde geweorces` · "the last of victory-times, of work in the world"; `sīðas[t]` and italic `a` of `sigehwīla` are Klaeber's changes (MS `siðas sige hwile`); Kemble, Grein, Grundtvig, Bugge, Trautmann each differ in the form (`-hwīl`, `-hwīle`, `-hwīla`); `worlde geweorces` construed as "in the world … of work", a guess.
- 2714 · `bealonīð(e)` · parenthesis marks the lost ending; Thorkelin transcripts `mð`, `niði`; taken as dative "with baleful malice", subject `attor`.
- 2716 · `wīshycgende` · "wise-thinking", rendered "thoughtful"; the shade is a guess.
- 2718–19 · `healde` · singular verb with plural `stānbogan`, kept; Holthausen `hēoldon`, and `ēcne` for `ēce`.
- 2721 · `till` · Zupitza saw an unexplained angle-shaped mark above the `t`; Klaeber prints plain.
- 2723 · `hel(m)` · MS/transcripts `helo`, `heb`; E. Sc. (after Grimm) `helm`; `onspēon` "unfastened".
- 2725 · `wælblēate` · "slaughter-wretched" (guess); Grein, Scheinert, Holthausen `-blāte` "deadly-pale".
- 2724 · `ofer benne` · "over the wound" kept; `ofer` could mean "despite" or "about".
- 2725–27 · `dæghwīla gedrogen hæfde, eorðan wynn(e)` · "lived through his day-times, earth's joy"; `wynn(e)` ending from Thorkelin and Grundtvig's transcript; the construction is loose.
- 2730–32 · `þǣr mē gifeðe swā … ǣnig yrfeweard … līce gelenge` · "if it were so granted me that any heir of my body should come"; `þǣr` "if", `wurde` subjunctive, `līce gelenge` "belonging to the body".
- 2736–37 · `mǣlgesceafta` · "time-fates"; hapax, guessed from `mǣl` + `gesceaft`.
- 2735–36 · `egesan ðeôn` · "to threaten with terror"; `ðeôn` read as the verb "press, urge"; exact sense a guess (cf. `egesan þȳwað` 1827).
- 2741 · `wītan` · "reproach, charge with" (not `witan` "know"), governing `morðọrbealo`.
- 2743 · `geong` · imperative of `gangan` (Kemble `gang`, Thorpe/Holthausen `gong`), not the adjective "young".
- 2746 · `swefeð` · "sleeps"; may be a euphemism for dead, or the dragon may be alive.
- 2748 · `gearo` · "ready" agreeing with `ic`; E., Aantekeningen `gearwe` "clearly".
- 2749 · `swegle searogimmas` · `swegle` read as adjective "bright" (guess from `swegl` "sky"); Thorpe `sigel`, Holthausen `siglu`, Rieger `sigle`.
